rewrites.blindSummary:
No trans-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is documented for this province. That absence records the absence of documented divergence — not local safety — because the national rules apply here unchanged.

Those rules, as documented: a judicial package leaked in October 2025 would criminalise conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality (up to three years) and same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies (up to four); raise the minimum age for gender-affirming healthcare from 18 to 25 behind a permanent-infertility mandate with government-hospital evaluations; and expose patients (up to three years) and providers (up to seven) to charges — protested by 15 LGBTI groups and the national medical association, with regional-court precedent cited against it. A long-standing national LGBTI monitor's 2025 report describes hostility becoming explicit official policy: 'family' directives to public institutions, the first closure of an LGBTI organisation in years, 6 right-to-life violations (3 hate-motivated killings), 89 torture or ill-treatment violations (51 in 2024), 313 liberty violations with 299 detention decisions, private-life violations rising 16 to 67 including blocked hormone therapy, 61 travel bans, expression violations 216 to 540, and 336 assembly violations.
rewrites.blindTangential: The draft judicial package's same-sex-ceremony and 'promotion' offences, and nationwide 'family' directives enforcing rainbow-symbol bans through public institutions, are LGB-adjacent instruments that shape how police treat gender-nonconforming people in this province too.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: Gender-marker registration through the civil registry, the restricted gender-affirming-care pathway, and the placement of trans detainees in men's facilities are resident-facing processes; visitors do not interact with them.
blindSourceSummaries: National-framework source (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): an international human-rights organisation's news release (29 October 2025) reports a leaked omnibus judicial draft that would amend the national penal code to criminalise conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' (up to three years in prison) and participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies (up to four years), and would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25 behind mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals; healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison and patients up to three years, with possible pretrial detention. Fifteen LGBT groups and the national medical association opposed the draft; the organisation warns it would force treatment underground and leave LGBT people in constant fear of arrest.

National-framework monitoring report (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): a long-standing national LGBTI monitor's 2025 review finds hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit official policy — 'family' directives issued to public institutions and the closure of an LGBTI+ rights organisation for the first time in years, with expression and artistic freedom restricted and events cancelled or banned. It documents 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings (trans people the most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51 the prior year), 313 liberty violations — about two and a half times the previous year — with 299 detention decisions, private-life violations rising from 16 to 67 including obstruction of trans people's hormone therapy, and 61 travel bans.

rewrites.blindSummary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): the province is consistently the country's most progressive on LGBT issues (first human-rights code inclusion 1992); a neighbourhood scene. Regional evidence: no hostile provincial legislation, but a documented 2023 wave of coordinated disruptions against public drag-storytime events at libraries — a municipal library in one locality postponed/cancelled repeatedly (a 14 January 2023 protest; a 13 October 2023 postponement) under 'public safety risk' claims, with a counter-gathering becoming the largest queer gathering the area had seen; at a library event in another locality with no police on scene a man pushed through to photograph the performer; a children's drag camp was threatened and required a public rally of support. Scored relative to the national score (0.86) for the country.
rewrites.blindTangential: The 2023 library drag-storytime disruption wave targets gender-nonconforming expression broadly (drag performers, children's events), not trans identity specifically; documented police non-presence at one library event signals thin protection for any gender-nonconforming visitor in comparable settings.
rewrites.blindOutOfScope: The national police-reported hate-crime statistics (658 sexual-orientation incidents in 2024) mix LGB and trans motivations and carry no provincial breakdown — treat as national climate context, not evidence of local risk.
blindSourceSummaries: A national statistics office release (30 March 2026) on police-reported hate crime in the country, 2024: 4,882 hate crimes reported, +1% from 2023 (which had risen 34% from 2022), more than doubling (+169%) since 2018; the rate per 100,000 population fell 2% to 11.9 incidents. Incidents targeting sexual orientation declined 26% to 658, while religion-motivated incidents were essentially stable at 1,342. No state/province-specific figures appear in the release (national context only).
Not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 307 redirect loop); the underlying report by a national advocacy organisation analyses 2024 hate-crime data affecting 2SLGBTQI people in the country.

An encyclopedia's country overview is the national framework that applies in this state/province under the country's charter of rights: it protects LGBTQ people from discrimination based on sexual orientation; sexual orientation has been covered at the national level since 1996 and gender identity and gender expression are protected under the national penal code's hate-propaganda and anti-discrimination provisions. A 2021 penal-code amendment, in force since 2022, made the country the first to statutorily ban conversion therapy nationwide for both minors and adults, and transgender people may change their legal gender in all state/province divisions under varying rules. The record's claims of no hostile provincial legislation and a national baseline score of 0.86 stand on this framework: charter equality protection, nationwide conversion-therapy criminalisation, and legal gender change availability in every state/province including this one.

rewrites.blindSummary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): a bohemian port-university culture; criminality is general rather than gender-targeted. Regional evidence: by a wide margin the country's highest-incidence region for anti-LGBTI discrimination — in 2024 it concentrated 51.32% of all national recorded cases (the second-ranked region at 25.12%), up 80.93% over 2023. In 2025 recorded cases fell here alongside the second-ranked region while all 14 other regions rose; the reporting advocacy group reads this as a decentralisation of hate toward state/province divisions with less LGBTIQ visibility and debate, not a local improvement. Scored relative to the national score (0.72) for the country.
rewrites.blindTangential: National-level hostility climate reaching the region: a parliamentary commission approved a report in May 2025 framing gender-affirming care for youth as harmful (recommending hormone bans for minors), giving political weight to stigmatising narratives that shape public hostility a visitor may encounter.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: Resident-facing: a national gender-identity support programme was excluded from the 2026 budget, cutting a national transition-care pathway; self-determination legal gender recognition is a national procedure.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's country page (12 March 2026): same-sex marriage and adoption legal since March 2022; since 2012 the country's hate-crime law has included sexual orientation and gender identity as aggravating circumstances and same-sex civil unions have been recognised since 2015; a 2019 comprehensive legal gender-recognition law is based on self-determination, and a third sex option has been available for intersex children on birth certificates since 2006. No legal ban exists on medically unnecessary interventions on minors, though the health ministry published non-binding intersex-affirming guidance in 2023; a 2020 family-court decision recognised two women as parents of a child born through assisted reproduction and a 2025 criminal court issued the country's first conviction in this field. National-framework source kept: the record claims the national score and no region-specific source covers the national framework this pass.

An advocacy group's annual human-rights report on sexual and gender diversity in this country (published March 2026, covering 2025): this region concentrated 51.32% of national recorded anti-LGBTI discrimination cases in 2024, up 80.93% over 2023; in 2025 cases fell only here and in the second-ranked region while all other regions rose; the group reads this as the decentralisation of hate toward state/province divisions where LGBTIQ themes have less visibility; the report carries the full per-region and per-commune series 2002-2025.

An encyclopedia's country overview is the national framework a visitor to this region stands under: a 2012 anti-discrimination law protects sexual orientation and gender identity, civil unions have been recognised since 2015, and same-sex marriage with full adoption rights has been legal since March 2022. A gender-identity law (introduced 2013, enacted 2018) has since 2019 let transgender people aged 14 and over change their name and gender on all official documents without surgery, and the armed forces admit LGBT personnel. Until 2022 the penal code set a higher age of consent of 18 for male homosexual acts; the constitutional court upheld the provision in a 5-5 vote in August 2018, and it was abolished in August 2022, equalising the age of consent.

An encyclopedia's Spanish-language overview of sexual diversity in this country carries four items directly relevant to this region: the first gathering of municipal diversity offices was held in 2022 in this region (the second in 2023 in another locality, the third in 2024 in yet another); one of this region's municipalities was among the founding members of a national network of municipalities with LGBTIQA+ offices or programmes created in 2014, a network that had grown beyond 60 municipalities by 2024; in April 2016 the first member of the national police force contracted a civil union with a same-sex partner; and in 2020 the national army formally incorporated its first transgender member. The same page confirms the national baseline: a 2012 anti-discrimination law, same-sex marriage under legislation promulgated 9 December 2021 and in force 10 March 2022, and a 2022 law banning discrimination based on sex characteristics for children and adolescents.
